Triggers.value: Being in a locked or confined room

Threat.value: I often react as if I am in danger even when nothing is actually wrong
My body feels constantly tense and ready to react to danger
My body reacts to danger before I have even had time to think

Memory.value: My memories of the frightening event are mostly pictures or images.
The memory forces its way into my mind when I do not want it to
Some moments of the event are extremely clear while others are completely blank

Negative Appraisals.value: I am no longer capable of doing the things that defined me
I can no longer trust my own body
My body keeps reacting as if I am still in danger even when I am safe

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Injustice: What happened to me was deeply unfair and nothing has been done about it
issues.explanation: For a life-threatening illness trauma, 'deeply unfair and nothing has been done about it' can be plausible, but in combination with global mistrust of people it shifts toward an interpersonal betrayal/assault formulation that is not supported by the rest of the profile. The memory and threat items describe somatic alarm and intrusive illness-related recollection, not a strong interpersonal trauma theme.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Mistrust: People can't be trusted
issues.explanation: 'People can't be trusted' is hard to reconcile with the stated trauma type of life-threatening illness unless there is clear evidence of medical betrayal, which is absent from the other selected items. It introduces an interpersonal threat meaning that is not reflected in the memory, threat, or trigger content.

For a 79-year-old woman with PTSD following life-threatening illness, the appraisal 'People can't be trusted' is hard to reconcile with the rest of the profile. The other endorsed items center on bodily danger, confinement/medical-context triggers, intrusive sensory memory, loss of capability, and distrust of one's body. A global interpersonal mistrust appraisal suggests betrayal/assault trauma or prominent social threat, but there are no corresponding triggers, memory themes, threat items, or strategies indicating interpersonal harm. This creates a cross-node and formulation mismatch: the active links strongly connect triggers, memory, appraisals, and threat around the illness experience, whereas this item introduces an unrepresented interpersonal theme.
